value: hearing thresholds declined steeply in a narrow band within the ultrasound, at 25 kHz (a second sensitivity peak in addition to the call-frequency peak)
method: summed auditory nerve responses recorded from the whole prothoracic leg nerve with tungsten hook electrodes; 50 ms tone pulses (1 ms rise/fall, 2 per second) from a speaker 50 cm away, calibrated at the cricket's position; levels stepped down from 90 dB SPL in 3 or 6 dB steps
conditions: laboratory preparation of 5 signalling males removed in 2006 from lek sites at The Nature Conservancy's Tallgrass Prairie Preserve, Osage County, Oklahoma; wings removed, ventral prothoracic cuticle opened to expose the leg nerve, animal waxed ventral side up; threshold = response amplitude more than 2 SD above non-auditory background, interpolated from intensity-response curves; recording temperature and any anaesthesia or chilling are not reported in the text read; N=5 animals, pooled curve; the same paper gives the highest sensitivity at the 2.0 kHz call carrier and the poorest at 10 kHz (the abstract and the Results differ slightly on those two values: abstract 41 dB SPL at 2 kHz and 84 dB at 10 kHz, Results 45.4 dB and 83 dB), so only the 25 kHz finding is filed

method: auditory evoked potentials (AEP) to tone pips at eight test frequencies, recorded with subdermal stainless steel electrodes from fish held in a mesh harness below the water surface above an underwater speaker; 2,000 repetitions per level, levels lowered in 5 dB steps; threshold = lowest level giving a repeatable AEP trace and a spectral peak at twice the stimulus frequency
conditions: wild fish caught by hook and line in Kaneohe Bay, Oahu, Hawaii, and tested in the laboratory; 6 males and 6 females in each of two seasons (spawning and non-spawning), 24 fish; fish not anaesthetised (MS-222 avoided because it can impair hair-cell function) but given an intramuscular pancuronium bromide injection to limit movement; water temperature not reported in the text read; sound pressure thresholds only; the same paper reports no sex difference and no seasonal difference in thresholds (Mann-Whitney, P>0.05), and notes that the 5 dB resolution of the AEP method may be unable to detect small differences; the AEP threshold is probably higher than the behavioural threshold
